_provenance.purpose: Cross-language Avro wire-compatibility fixture for conduit.schema.AvroSchema (WS2). A Python-only round-trip is not evidence of Go interop, so both directions are recorded and independently verified: go_avro_hex is what avro.Marshal actually produces today (re-derived and compared by tools/avro_fixture_gen's verify mode, which fails CI if the committed bytes drift), and python_avro_hex is fastavro schemaless_writer output for the same value, which the same Go verifier decodes back to the expected value.
_provenance.go_codec: github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.34.0 -- the maintained fork of hamba/avro/v2 that conduit-commons' schema/avro package (Serde) wraps directly (conduit-commons#279 replaced the archived hamba module with this fork; same codec, plain headerless Avro binary). See tools/avro_fixture_gen/main.go.
_provenance.generator_note: go_avro_hex: avro.ParseBytes(schema) + avro.Marshal(schema, value) via tools/avro_fixture_gen -emit; python_avro_hex: fastavro.schemaless_writer. Both verified by `go run . -fixture tests/testdata/avro_golden.json` (re-derives go_avro_hex and decodes python_avro_hex to the expected value). Regenerate go_avro_hex with -emit, python_avro_hex with fastavro, then run the verifier before committing.
_provenance.map_nondeterminism_note: No map field is included in this schema deliberately: Go's avro.Marshal iterates Go map entries in randomized order, so a record with a non-empty map field is nondeterministic on the Go side -- byte-compatible across languages is impossible by construction there (decode still works; this is a Go-side property, not a Python one). Array block framing below is deterministic in both encoders; maps would frame the same way.
_provenance.array_framing_note: Avro's array block framing permits two spec-legal styles: a plain positive item count, or a negative count paired with an explicit byte-size prefix (for reader skip-ahead). iskorotkov/avro (like hamba before it) emits the size-prefixed form for non-empty blocks; fastavro emits the plain form. Both are mutually decodable -- the Go verifier decodes python_avro_hex for every case, and the Python tests decode go_avro_hex -- but the two encoders' bytes are not identical for schemas containing a non-empty array field (case with_note). Case null_note has an empty array block (count 0 in either style), so it is fully byte-exact in both directions.
